paper.title: Learning to Optimize Via Posterior Sampling

settings.name_in_paper: Finitely many actions, R_t in [0,1], arbitrary prior
unmapped: arbitrary dependence among action rewards via a general prior over reward functions
available action sets A_t subset of A may be random and change over time
settings.definition_quote: We consider in this section a problem with $|\mathcal{A}| < \infty$ actions and rewards satisfying $R_t \in [0,1]$ for all $t$ almost surely. ... we make no further assumptions on the class of reward functions $\mathcal{F}$ or on the prior distribution over $\theta$.

unmapped: learner knows the prior over theta
settings.definition_quote: If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle$ ..., $\sup_{\rho \in \Theta} \|\rho\|_2 \leq c_1$, and $\sup_{a \in \mathcal{A}} \|\phi(a)\|_2 \leq c_2$, and for each $t$, $R_t - f_{\theta}(A_t)$ conditioned on $(H_t, A_t, \theta)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian

unmapped: inverse link g strictly increasing, continuously differentiable; r = ratio of max to min slope of g
settings.definition_quote: In a generalized linear model, the reward function takes the form $f_{\theta}(a) := g\left(  \left\langle \phi(a), \theta\ \right\rangle\right)$ where the inverse link function $g$ is strictly increasing and continuously differentiable.

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian process prior, finite action set
unmapped: reward function drawn from a Gaussian process with marginal variances bounded by 1
settings.definition_quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, $\left( f_\theta(a):  a\in \mathcal{A} \right)$ follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution with marginal variances bounded by $1$, $R_t-f_{\theta}(A_t)$ is independent of $(H_t, \theta, A_t)$, and ... iid sequence of zero-mean Gaussian random variables with variance $\sigma^{2}$

settings.name_in_paper: General function class F with bounded rewards and sub-Gaussian noise
unmapped: mean reward function lies in a known class F with f(a) in [0,C]
complexity measured by eluder dimension and Kolmogorov dimension
settings.definition_quote: For all $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and $a \in \mathcal{A}$, $f(a) \in [0,C]$. ... For all $t \in \mathbb{N}$, $R_t-f_{\theta}(A_t)$ conditioned on $(H_t, \theta, A_t)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian.

algorithms.name: Posterior sampling with initial designed exploration (pi^IPS_{a_1..a_d})

source.label: prop:finite
source.quote: If $|\mathcal{A}|=K<\infty$ and $R_t \in [0,1]$, then for any $T\in \mathbb{N}$ \mathrm{BayesRegret}(T, \pi^{\mathrm{PS}}) \leq 2\min\{K, T\}+4\sqrt{K T(2+6\log(T))}.

results.notes: Holds for any prior; posterior sampling does not use T, so anytime.

source.label: prop:linear
source.quote: Fix positive constants $\sigma$, $c_1$, and $c_2$. If $\Theta\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $f_\theta(a)=\left\langle \phi(a), \theta \right\rangle$ ..., then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) = O(d \log T \sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Derived from analysis of Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2011 via regret decomposition; proof only sketched. Linear models example in Section 6 restates the same O(d sqrt(T) log T) bound via eluder dimension.

symbols.E_sqrt_l0: E[sqrt(||theta||_0)], expected square root of the number of nonzero components of theta under the prior

results.notes: Sparse linear bound derived from Abbasi-Yadkori et al. 2012; proof sketched.

conditions: exist a_1..a_d with sum phi(a_i)phi(a_i)^T >= lambda I

source.label: prop:generalizedLinear
source.quote: Fix positive constants $c_1$, $c_2$, $C$, and $\lambda$. If ... $\mathcal{A}_t = \mathcal{A}$ for all $t$, $\sum_{i=1}^{d} \phi(a_i) \phi(a_i)^T \succeq \lambda I$ for some $a_1,\ldots,a_d \in \mathcal{A}$, and $R_t \in [0,C]$ for all $t$, then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm IPS}_{a_1,\ldots,a_d}\right) = O(r d \log^{3/2} T \sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Derived from Filippi et al. 2010 analysis; proof sketched.

conditions: marginal prior variances of f_theta(a) bounded by 1
noise iid Gaussian with variance sigma^2, independent of (H_t, theta, A_t)

source.quote: If $\mathcal{A}$ is finite, $\left( f_\theta(a):  a\in \mathcal{A} \right)$ follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution with marginal variances bounded by $1$, ... then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right)\leq 1+2\sqrt{T \gamma_T \ln\left(1+\sigma^{-2}\right)^{-1} \ln\left(\frac{(T^2+1) \left| \mathcal{A}\right|} {\sqrt{2\pi}} \right)}$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: K = |A|; sigma_std is the Gaussian noise standard deviation; gamma_T is maximum information gain.

symbols.C_rng: bound C on mean rewards, f(a) in [0,C]
symbols.beta_star: confidence parameter beta*_T(F, delta, alpha) = 8 sigma^2 log(N(F,alpha,||.||_inf)/delta) + 2 alpha T (8C + sqrt(8 sigma^2 ln(4T^2/delta)))

source.label: prop: Bayesian regret bound in terms of beta
source.number: Proposition (prop: Bayesian regret bound in terms of beta)
source.quote: For all $T \in \mathbb{N}$, $\alpha > 0$ and $\delta \leq 1/2T$, ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+ \left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C +4\sqrt{{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \beta^{*}_{T} \left(\mathcal{F}, \alpha, \delta \right) T}.$

results.notes: delta and alpha here are analysis parameters, not algorithm inputs.

bound.expression_latex: 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T}

symbols.C_rng: bound C on mean rewards, f(a) in [0,C]
symbols.o_1: a term vanishing as T -> infinity

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: For any fixed class of functions $\mathcal{F}$, ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C+ 16\sigma \sqrt{  {\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F},  T^{-1} \right) \left(1+o(1)+{\rm dim}_K\left(\mathcal{F} \right) \right) \log(T) T}$ for all $T\in \mathbb{N}$.

results.notes: Contains o(1) term; specializes to O(d sqrt(T) log T) for linear models (example).

symbols.C_rng: bound C on mean rewards, f(a) in [0,C]
symbols.F_card: cardinality |F| of the finite function class

source.label: prop: risk bound
source.quote: Further, if $\mathcal{F}$ is finite then ${\rm BayesRegret}\left(T,\,\pi^{\rm PS}\right) \leq 1+\left[{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right)+1\right]C +8\sigma\sqrt{2{\rm dim}_E\left(\mathcal{F}, T^{-1} \right) \log\left(2\left|\mathcal{F}\right|T\right)T},$ for all $T \in \mathbb{N}$.

symbols.r: ratio between maximal and minimal slope of g

conditions: g increasing Lipschitz; bounded feature and parameter norms

source.quote: Consider the case of a $d$-dimensional generalized linear model ... Proposition \ref{prop: risk bound} yields an $O(rd\sqrt{T} \log (rT))$ Bayesian regret bound.

results.notes: Stated in an example, derived from Proposition (prop: risk bound) with eluder-dimension bound from the appendix; standard posterior sampling without designed exploration.
